paper_title: The Unseen Targets of Hate -- A Systematic Review of Hateful   Communication Datasets
caption: Conceptualized and operationalized targets by year along with the distribution of datasets. Targeted refers to datasets that have explicitly mentioned at least one target in their construct definition (i.e., in the conceptualization phase) and/or publications in which the authors define concrete measures to ensure and validate the presence of at least one target group in the data (i.e., in the operationalization phase). Untargeted refers to all other datasets that do not meet these two criteria. Note that the data for 2022 is only partially available (as described in our Methods and Data Section).
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the annual distribution of datasets from 2012 to 2022, categorized by whether they are “Targeted” or “Untargeted” in their conceptualization and operationalization of hate speech targets, as defined in the paper “The Unseen Targets of Hate.” The horizontal axis represents the year, ranging from 2012 to 2022, while the vertical axis indicates the “Number of datasets,” scaled from 0 to 160 in increments of 20. Each year is represented by a stacked bar, with the lower segment in blue denoting “Untargeted” datasets and the upper segment in orange representing “Targeted” datasets. In 2012, only one dataset is shown, entirely “Targeted.” From 2013 to 2015, the number of datasets remains low, with mostly “Targeted” entries. A noticeable increase begins in 2016 (12 total datasets: 2 Untargeted, 10 Targeted), rising steadily through 2019 (66 total: 12 Untargeted, 54 Targeted), 2020 (132 total: 50 Untargeted, 82 Targeted), and peaking in 2021 with 160 total datasets (70 Untargeted, 90 Targeted). In 2022, the total drops to 40 datasets (10 Untargeted, 30 Targeted), which the caption notes is partial data. The chart visually emphasizes the growing volume of datasets over time and the increasing proportion of “Targeted” datasets, especially from 2018 onward, though “Untargeted” datasets also grow in absolute number. The legend in the top-left corner clarifies the color coding, and the stacked bar format allows for comparison of both total dataset counts per year and the relative contribution of each category.
